title: Separating mixing from selection: a leave-one-line-out benchmark and an audit protocol for cross-cell-line perturbation evaluation
description: Analysis code and derived per-target scores for a leave-one-line-out benchmark of cross-cell-line perturbation prediction. Tier A holds out each of four harmonized cell lines (K562, RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat; 5,486 queries); Tier B holds out each of five heterogeneous lines (H1, K562, RPE1, HCT116, HEK293T; 18,678 queries). The drug panel covers seven to twelve Tahoe-100M lines on 648 or 646 shared conditions, including the twelve-line robustness analyses. Version 1.3.3 is the Briefings in Bioinformatics submission revision: the main text was condensed to 6,855 narrative words with a 248-word abstract, the supplementary material moved to a separate source file, and the funding statement names the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 12305381); results, figures, and tables are unchanged from 1.3.2. Version 1.3.2 is a language revision of the manuscript text; no number, citation, figure, or table changed. Version 1.3.1 rescored the Tahoe coherence and drug-exclusion artifacts with a bounded tie-midrank rule, regenerated the coherence figure and its partial correlations, moved the scGPT comparison to Supplementary Figure S1, renumbered figures, and added a graphical abstract and key points. Version 1.3.0 added metric positive and negative controls, a candidate-pool composition control, and an independent DESeq2 truth-table confirmation for 150 H1 targets, and it regenerated the genetic budget, exchange, and allocation artifacts with the corrected scorer. The archive contains the analysis scripts, summary tables, manuscript source, figures, and the per-target arrays needed to rerun the headline audit. The largest prediction arrays and raw row caches are deposited as separate files. The analysis code is MIT-licensed; derived data and figures are CC BY 4.0. Raw third-party datasets are not redistributed and remain under their original licenses.
